title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO LTD
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium bromide framework. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The capacity retention of 92% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

title: Amperometric nitrogen oxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide comprises a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The nitrogen oxide sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 700 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to nitrogen oxide against interfering gases. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The limiting current is proportional to the nitrogen oxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 700 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The lithium sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises iron sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The active material iron sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. A lithium-sulfur battery with the iron sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1100 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer.
