A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte stable above 4.8 V
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising sulfur and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a sulfur core and a conductive carbon shell. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. A precursor of the LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 75% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The Li3N layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: iron sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The LiF layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tungsten and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the moisture stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Amperometric hydrogen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the hydrogen concentration into an ionic activity. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The solid electrolyte of sodium beta-alumina conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The hydrogen sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The gold electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising sodium beta-alumina, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3YCl6. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V.
