An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 87% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. With 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises lithium sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The lithium sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 8 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.2 W/cm2. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The stack of 50 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The reversible cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 8 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A precursor of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. In the trigonal structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent.
