In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The stack of 50 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte for detecting nitrogen oxide
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the nitrogen oxide concentration into an ionic activity. The sensor operating at 400 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for nitrogen oxide. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 400 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of nitrogen oxide concentration at 400 degrees C. The gold electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; a sensing electrode comprising gold disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 400 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum fluoride conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A precursor of the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less.
