abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state lithium battery. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 700 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to ammonia against interfering gases. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 700 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and LiI to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the interfacial resistance is retained.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The LLZO and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1100 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The sheet thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the molybdenum disulfide cathode. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivering 1400 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: titanium disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V.
