A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the ammonia concentration into an ionic activity. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 500 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects ammonia.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the niobium capacitor. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The 100 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Mixed potential type ammonia sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 300 degrees C. The sensor detects ammonia with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects ammonia.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The resulting Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. With 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxygen content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The sheet thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The resulting LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 86% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
