A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous aluminum anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The 47 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) is doped with p-toluenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 8 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The capacitor has a capacitance of 47 microfarads, a rated voltage of 35 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 8 milliohms at 100 kHz. The p-toluenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with p-toluenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 8 milliohms or less.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With hafnium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 120 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
