abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the moisture stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free self-supporting sulfide ion-conductive solid sheet bound by a fibrillated fluoropolymer network and method of forming the same
abstract: A self-supporting sheet comprises particles of an argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid of the Li6PS5Cl type and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt%, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without any solvent. The sheet is formed by kneading the powder and the binder under a shear rate of 200 s^-1 to 800 s^-1 at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C so that the binder is fibrillized, rolling the kneaded mass between a pair of rollers heated to 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and calendering the rolled film in at least three passes with a stepwise reduced roller gap to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, and the sheet has a porosity of 8% or less, a tensile strength of 1.5 MPa or more, and an ionic conductivity of 2.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because no polar solvent contacts the sulfide, the conductivity of the powder is retained, and the sheet can be wound on a roll and laminated onto an electrode without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability in production and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A self-supporting sheet comprising: particles of a sulfide ion-conductive solid having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt% relative to the sheet, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, the sheet is free of a solvent, and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 8% or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. A 5 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The stack of 50 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
