The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The tin content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

assignee: Industry-Academic Cooperation Foundation of Seodam National University
title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A precursor of the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. With 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A precursor of the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and production method thereof
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the moisture stability of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. With 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material.
