first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone is also described. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 3 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Potentiometric hydrogen sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a platinum electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the hydrogen concentration. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for hydrogen. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a lanthanum fluoride solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 400 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The sensor shows a response time of 5 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Germanium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life and interfacial resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. With zirconium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, ErBr3, and TiBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium.
