A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium bis(oxalato)borate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. With 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt%.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Composite cathode comprising sulfur and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 94% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%.
