A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a tin source at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LLZO material. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. With 2 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LATP and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 5 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a aluminum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Mixed potential type nitrogen oxide sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the nitrogen oxide concentration. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of nitrogen oxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensor with a response time of 20 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for nitrogen oxide. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor detects nitrogen oxide with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The mixed halogen substitution improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide comprises a yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The protective layer improves the durability of the yttria-stabilized zirconia sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor detects carbon dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. The sensor with a response time of 20 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for carbon dioxide. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 400 degrees C. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the solid electrolyte powder with the indium additive in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode.
