Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. With 2 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 88% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises lithium sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which molybdenum disulfide is confined in the pores of carbon nanotubes to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a lithium secondary battery. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Amperometric oxygen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the oxygen concentration into an ionic activity. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of oxygen concentration at 300 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects oxygen.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing alumina nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
