abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Composite cathode comprising molybdenum disulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 10 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 700 to 850 degrees C is described. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 700 to 850 degrees C. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The LiF and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 86% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: tantalum solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor has a capacitance of 470 microfarads, a rated voltage of 25 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 5 milliohms at 100 kHz. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the tantalum capacitor. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The dispersion of polypyrrole gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 470 microfarad rating. The capacitor rated at 25 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a tantalum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 25 V.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. With 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
