A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Al2O3 inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The bilayer structure improves the sinterability and moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NAT UNIV IND ACAD COOP FOUND
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved high-voltage stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 92% or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the sheet formability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 97%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid is described. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
