The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 92% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and method for preparing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The LiF, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The LiPON layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The resulting Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises molybdenum disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 3 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 500 to 650 degrees C is described. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: molybdenum disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The resulting Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and carboxymethyl cellulose binder
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, porous carbon, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the solid electrolyte powder with the magnesium additive in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 86% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1.
