A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the interfacial resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the interfacial resistance is retained.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for carbon dioxide with improved response time
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The multilayer structure with the lanthanum fluoride ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects carbon dioxide.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising sulfur and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with an indium additive. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A lithium-sulfur battery with the nickel sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode delivering 1400 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises molybdenum disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 2 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which sulfur is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: titanium disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a titanium disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. With 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In the monoclinic structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

assignee: DRIOSTUS ADVANCED MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a platinum electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the nitrogen oxide concentration. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor detects nitrogen oxide with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the nitrogen oxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Amperometric hydrogen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 400 degrees C. The sensor with a response time of 2 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for hydrogen.
