A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium difluorophosphate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. In the trigonal structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a titanium disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, graphene, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A precursor of the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery.
