A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LLZO material. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The warm isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a platinum electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the ammonia concentration. The sensor shows a response time of 5 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 300 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor with a response time of 5 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for ammonia. The auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate makes the sensor selective to ammonia against interfering gases. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 300 degrees C.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The dispersion of polyaniline gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 220 microfarad rating. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. The capacitor rated at 16 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The polyaniline is doped with naphthalenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ion-conductive solid shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiBr, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The LiF layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The resulting Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. The Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The LLZO, LATP, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The uniaxial pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance.
