The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiBr, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 88% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide comprises a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising platinum, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the nitrogen oxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth.
