The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The active material sulfur is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising sulfur and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the interfacial resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4.

title: Amperometric nitrogen oxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the nitrogen oxide concentration into an ionic activity. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for nitrogen oxide. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the nitrogen oxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of nitrogen oxide.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Sulfide glass ceramic solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 crystal phase with controlled crystallinity and widened electrochemical window
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte is a glass ceramic in which a Li7P3S11 crystal phase is precipitated in a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 70:30 and containing LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%. A glass obtained by mechanical amorphization of the raw materials in a planetary mill is heat-treated at 260 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours, just above the crystallization onset, so that the metastable Li7P3S11 phase precipitates with a crystallite size of 30 nm to 150 nm while devitrification to the low-conductivity Li4P2S6 phase is kept to 3% or less. The degree of crystallinity is 60% to 85%, the residual glassy phase deforms plastically during cold pressing, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C with an activation energy of 0.22 eV. The iodide widens the electrochemical window on the reduction side to 1.6 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic is distinguished from crystalline Li6PS5Cl or Li3PS4 powders by the presence of the vitreous phase and gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte comprising: a vitreous phase comprising Li2S and P2S5; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the vitreous phase, wherein a degree of crystallinity determined by X-ray diffraction is 40% to 95%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Mixed potential type carbon dioxide sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which carbon dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of carbon dioxide concentration at 400 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of carbon dioxide.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The LATP and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a titanium disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The titanium disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled.
