Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and vinylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell. A 5 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

assignee: University Of Selexen INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC Cooperation Foundation
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window of the solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of ketjen black to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The LLTO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The LiF and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing alumina nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization.
