title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium bis(oxalato)borate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. With 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ErBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). The Al2O3 layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li3YCl6 material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and cycle life of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The LiNbO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Potentiometric oxygen sensor having an auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which oxygen is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen. The oxygen sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising barium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects oxygen.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating.
