A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The silicon substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and LiI to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises sulfur impregnated in carbon nanotubes and a carbon coating on the composite. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The active material sulfur is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The confinement of sulfur in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of ketjen black to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a lanthanum strontium manganite electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the ammonia concentration. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to ammonia against interfering gases. The sensor detects ammonia with high selectivity and a response time of 10 seconds.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which sulfur is confined in the pores of carbon nanotubes to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The carbon coating on the sulfur composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In the trigonal structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Negative electrode structure with a lithium fluoride and magnesium nucleation additive layer for suppressing dendrites in a solid-state lithium cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a solid-state lithium cell comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer comprising Li3PS4 or a garnet-type LLZO, and a nucleation additive layer disposed between them, the additive layer comprising lithium fluoride particles having an average size of 50 nm to 300 nm and magnesium particles in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 90:10 and having a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. During plating, lithium alloys with the magnesium to form uniformly distributed nucleation sites, while the lithium fluoride, which has an electronic conductivity below 1 x 10^-10 S/cm, blocks electron leakage into the ion-conductive solid and prevents the growth of lithium filaments along grain boundaries. During stripping, the alloy phase keeps the contact so that void formation at the interface is suppressed under a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 8 MPa. The structure raises the critical current density at 25 degrees C from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2.5 mA/cm2 or more, lowers the interfacial resistance to 10 ohm cm2 or less, and keeps the ionic conductivity of the interface. A symmetric cell with the structure survives 500 plating and stripping cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 without short circuit with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% or more.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a solid-state lithium cell, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive layer disposed between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer, the additive layer comprising a lithium halide and a metal that forms an alloy with lithium.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which sulfur is confined in the pores of porous carbon to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The active material sulfur is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The confinement of sulfur in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The cathode delivering 1200 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
