abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a sulfur core and a conductive carbon shell. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. The carbon coating on the sulfur composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a iron sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. A lithium-sulfur battery with the iron sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state lithium battery. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: iron sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. A power module combining the capacitor with a lithium battery is also described. The dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 220 microfarad rating.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with naphthalenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The arsenic-free antimony content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6.
