A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a lanthanum fluoride solid electrolyte for detecting nitrogen oxide
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 300 degrees C. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of nitrogen oxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The protective layer improves the durability of the lanthanum fluoride sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 45% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tantalum oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: High-conductivity argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor with a lithium-deficient composition and an impurity-free diffraction pattern
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a lithium-deficient composition represented by Li(6-x-y)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.5 and 0 < y <= 0.15, the lithium deficiency y being introduced by adding P2S5 in a slight excess so that lithium vacancies are created on the 48h site. The anion disorder between the sulfur and chlorine sites is 40% or more, no diffraction peak attributable to LiCl, Li3PS4, or Li2S is observed, and the lattice parameter is 9.80 angstroms to 9.86 angstroms. The combination of the vacancies and the anion disorder gives an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C for a cold-pressed pellet and 9 mS/cm or more for a pellet sintered at 500 degrees C, together with an activation energy of 0.26 eV or less. The material is crystalline and is not a glass ceramic, so that its conductivity does not decrease upon storage at 60 degrees C.
