A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; nickel sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiBr, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and carboxymethyl cellulose binder
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, graphene, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Composite cathode comprising molybdenum disulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises molybdenum disulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a lithium secondary battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. With 1 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A precursor of the Li3YCl6 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the sodium beta-alumina sensor in an exhaust gas. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising sodium beta-alumina, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The silicon content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 35 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a nickel sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The resulting Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.
