title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 93% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tungsten oxide with a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
