abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The capacity retention of 92% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polycarbonate based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid is described. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the molybdenum disulfide cathode. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a gallium oxide with a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Potentiometric nitrogen oxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the nitrogen oxide concentration into an ionic activity. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of nitrogen oxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for nitrogen oxide.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid.
